page: Amazon Web Services c6a.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7R13 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. It features 16 vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.6 GHz. The instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It runs on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware. Network connectivity is supported by a 6 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong single-core CPU performance, as demonstrated by a stress-ng single-core score of 2993.35. Multi-core performance falls within the average tier, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 23946.82 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 9683.0. A notable performance tradeoff exists in memory bandwidth; while cached small-block read operations are average at 1140.64 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write operations are weak, measuring 39.28 GB/sec and 21.76 GB/sec respectively. Small-model LLM text generation performs strongly at 300.58 tokens/sec, while medium-model inference speeds remain average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the c6a.4xlarge offers a balanced compute-to-memory ratio for workloads requiring dedicated CPU resources without the overhead of local storage or specialized accelerators. The instance is suitable for compute-heavy tasks such as software compilation, web serving, single-threaded compression tasks, and moderate database operations. However, workloads requiring high uncached memory throughput or local NVMe storage may experience bottlenecks.
